packages.name: nova
packages.description: Nova itself: the kernel and the system every app runs on
packages.title: Nova
packages.about:
Updates Nova on the disk it was installed on. The new version starts at the next restart; the one you have now stays in the boot menu as "Nova (previous version)", in case the new one misbehaves. Your apps, settings and files aren't touched.
A Nova running from a USB stick is updated by writing a new image to the stick.

changes.notes: - ext2 reads neighbouring blocks of a file in one disk request
- L1: the profiler says what holds the kernel lock, and times input to the screen
- The desktop's processor's interrupts go ahead for the kernel lock too
- With four processors or more, the first is the desktop's alone
- The desktop goes ahead of the other processors for the kernel lock
- NVK sees the system memory that is free; wine 11.0-13, nvidia-vulkan 26.2.6-29
- Wine with GnuTLS: public keys, certificates' signatures and TLS (wine 11.0-12)
- Vulkan surfaces that find their window later; Wine's driver makes them so
- libc: the SIOCGIF* ioctls in a file of their own
- Drawing in another process's window (SYS_WIN_PUT); Vulkan and Wine's driver use it
- libc: struct ifreq and the SIOCGIF* ioctls; Wine's nsiproxy builds, wine 11.0-9
- Another process's memory read and written (SYS_PROCESS_VM); Wine's server uses it
- A signal to one thread of another process (SYS_TKILL's tgid); Wine's server uses it
- Vulkan: several instances at once; Wine: the server survives a cancel that completes at once
- Folders read many entries a call (SYS_READDIRS); Wine finds Nova's root certificates
- Writable shared mappings of files on a disk, and msync
- kill reaches a process whose first thread has left; nvidia-vulkan 26.2.6-25
- NVK on NVIDIA's driver: each flush's semaphore release in its own place (the Xid 32 freezes)
- NVK on NVIDIA's driver: write-combining buffers flushed before the card is told of work
- Wine as a package: ports/wine/build.sh, the wine command, tests/wine-package.sh
- 12.8, the build side: a Vulkan surface for Windows windows, Wine with libvulkan, DXVK fetched
- A window's own icon (SYS_WIN_SET_ICON), and a dock tile for programs that are not apps
- Popup windows (NV_WIN_POPUP), and Wine's menus in them
- ext2: as many files open at once as programs open
- mmap by address reaches up to the stack, and the stack's place reads as taken
- 12.3: arch_prctl's base holds when %fs still has a 32-bit selector
- 12.3: set_thread_area, and segment registers that go with the thread
- 12.3: Linux's user segment selectors, and a 64-bit program runs 32-bit code
- Fault codes as Linux gives them, real inode numbers on ext2, a prefix without z:
- Wine 12.5: address space by request, socket names that stat, staging; first Windows images load

packages.name: nvidia
packages.description: NVIDIA's open GPU driver, for GeForce RTX 30 and 40 cards (first stage: it starts the GPU)
packages.title: NVIDIA Graphics
packages.about:
NVIDIA's open-source GPU driver, for GeForce RTX 30 and 40 series cards (RTX 3050 to 4090). Nova loads it when it starts, if it finds one of these cards.
This is the first stage: the driver starts the card and its firmware, and writes what it found to /var/log/nvidia.log. The screen is still drawn the way it was; using the card for drawing comes later.
If Nova ever stops while starting it, the next start skips it by itself (and says so), until a new version comes. modules=off in /etc/nova.conf turns every driver from a package off.

changes.notes: - Task Manager gets a GPU tab: how busy the card is (drawing, memory, video decoding and encoding), its video memory and its performance state. Needs the Nova update published with it.
- Programs can map system memory the card uses (it was refused as "not supported"): Vulkan (NVIDIA Vulkan's vktest) needs it to start the card.
- Programs can map the card's memory (video memory and system memory it uses) and write to it directly, as graphics libraries do; nvidia-info checks it. Needs the Nova update published with it.
- When the monitor is switched off and on again (or its cable unplugged and plugged back in), the picture comes back: the mode is set again.

- Settings > Display's resolutions go down as well as up (they were listed biggest first).
- Switches on the card's own sound device for HDMI and DisplayPort, so Settings > Sound can play through your monitor or TV (needs the Nova update published with it).
- Fixes the black screen: the display's output scale was left at zero, which turns every pixel black.

- If the display setup fails partway, the screen is given back to the old display instead of staying black.
- The last start's log is kept as /var/log/nvidia.log.1, and the log says more about each display step.

- The display: NVIDIA's display driver sets your monitor to its own resolution and refresh rate, and Nova's desktop draws through the graphics card. Settings > Display lists the monitor's modes.
- The first time, it's a trial: press Keep in Settings > Display. If the screen stayed black and you couldn't, the next start goes back to the old display by itself.
- Needs the Nova update published with it.

- Programs can talk to the driver: /dev/nvidiactl and /dev/nvidia0, as on Linux. The nvidia-info command (in the Terminal) asks it for the card's name, memory and the driver's version. Needs the Nova update published with it.

- When the driver waits for something another part of it does (its interrupt work, queued work, timers), that work now runs while it waits, instead of the wait being skipped. Waits that never end are logged with where they were.
- The card's interrupts are connected (MSI): the driver's check that they arrive stopped it before. Needs the Nova update published with it.
- First test: finds the card, starts NVIDIA's driver and the card's firmware, and writes what happened to /var/log/nvidia.log.

packages.name: nvidia-vulkan
packages.description: Vulkan and OpenGL for NVIDIA cards (Mesa's NVK and Zink, Google's ANGLE): vktest, gltest and zinktest check the card, vkcube and glcube spin cubes
packages.title: NVIDIA Vulkan
packages.about:
Vulkan, the 3D and compute interface, for GeForce RTX 30 and 40 cards: Mesa's open NVK driver, on NVIDIA's driver (the NVIDIA Graphics package).
Two programs to try in the Terminal: vktest lists the card, runs a small program on it, draws a triangle and saves it as vktest.png in your home folder (its last line says VKTEST PASS or what failed); vkcube opens a window with a spinning cube the card draws, and prints its frame rate; gltest draws a triangle with OpenGL ES through ANGLE, as the browser's WebGL does, and saves it as gltest.png (GLTEST PASS or what failed); zinktest draws one with OpenGL 4 through Mesa's Zink, as ported programs do, and saves it as zinktest.png (ZINKTEST PASS or what failed); glcube spins a cube with OpenGL in a window you can resize (F11: fullscreen), and prints its frame rate.

changes.notes: - Vulkan sees how much system memory is free (it thought a few megabytes), so programs that keep to its budget can use it.
- A Vulkan surface can be made before its window exists and find it later (Wine uses this).
- Vulkan can show its picture in a window that belongs to another program (a helper process drawing for the program that made the window).
- A program that uses Vulkan in two places at once (two instances) no longer ends when it closes the newer one first.
- Fixes Vulkan and OpenGL programs freezing now and then with their picture stopped (the graphics card could be told that work was finished too soon).

- Vulkan and OpenGL windows (vkcube, glcube) show a frame each time the monitor refreshes, in step with the desktop, instead of every 15 ms: no more dropped frames. Needs the Nova update published with it.
- The Store shows what each version changed (this list).
- OpenGL windows use colors a window can show (8 bits a channel), so glcube's cube appears instead of a blank window.
- Vulkan windows take images in RGBA order too, as OpenGL (Zink) asks for them.
- Programs that use the card from several threads at once (OpenGL in a window does) no longer get in each other's way.

- OpenGL in windows: glcube spins a cube in a window you can resize (F11: fullscreen; glcube -i: as fast as it goes).
- Vulkan windows follow their window's size when it changes. Needs the Nova update published with it.
- zinktest finds its OpenGL settings on the card (it found none).
- OpenGL (Zink) starts on the card: it stopped with "out of host memory".
- OpenGL for ported programs, through Mesa's Zink on Vulkan: zinktest draws a triangle with OpenGL 4 and checks it.
- gltest sets up the card's memory as the browser does, so the browser's WebGL starts instead of crashing.
- OpenGL ES through Google's ANGLE, as the browser's WebGL uses it: gltest draws a triangle and checks it.

- vkcube and other Vulkan windows show a frame each time the desktop draws one, instead of hundreds nobody sees.
- vktest no longer ends with two error lines from the driver.
- Vulkan programs that wait for the card with timeline semaphores (the browser's drawing) work.
- Programs that ask Vulkan for layers (the browser does) get an answer.
- vkcube's frame rate lines appear as they're printed.
- vkcube draws the cube's front faces (it showed the inside).
- Vulkan for programs, with windows: vkcube spins a cube in a window and prints its frame rate.
- vktest's shaders compile for the card.
- When vktest fails, it shows what NVIDIA's driver said.
- Vulkan can use the computer's memory for the card, as NVIDIA's driver requires.
- The card is set up the way Mesa expects.
- Vulkan's functions are all in place in a program (some were missing).
- vktest says where Vulkan stopped when it fails.
- First test: vktest, Vulkan through Mesa's NVK on NVIDIA's driver. It lists the card, runs a small program on it, draws a triangle and saves it as vktest.png.

packages.name: wine
packages.description: Wine: run Windows programs (early: a command, no app yet)
packages.title: Wine
packages.about:
Runs programs made for Windows, 64-bit and 32-bit, in windows of their own with sound: type wine and the program's name in the Terminal (wine notepad, wine winecfg, or a .exe in your home folder).
The first start sets up a Windows folder in your home folder (.wine), which takes a few minutes.
DirectX through the graphics card (wine --dxvk) needs the NVIDIA driver and Vulkan packages.
This is an early version: games and Steam are not expected to work yet. It needs Nova installed on a disk, not started from a USB stick.

changes.notes: - Text drawn with DirectWrite shows: Steam's windows (and other programs built on Chromium) had no letters in them.
- DirectX programs get the system memory they ask for: the graphics driver thought only a few megabytes were free. Steam ended just after signing in because of it.
- Windows programs can check certificates and signatures and make secure (https) connections: Wine has GnuTLS now. Steam needs this to reach its logon servers.
- A program that prepares its picture before its window is shown (Chromium, so Steam's windows) shows it once the window is there, and keeps showing it when the window is resized.
- A program whose picture is drawn by a helper process (Chromium does this, so Steam's windows) shows it: the helper can draw in the program's window. Needs the Nova update published with it.
- Windows programs can ask about the network: the computer's network cards and addresses, and which program owns a connection. Steam asks that before it lets its own window talk to it.
- Windows programs can read and change another program's memory, and their own through the same call, as Steam's web helper does when it starts. Needs the Nova update published with it.

- Steam gets further: three faults that stopped its helpers are fixed (a program using the graphics card twice over ended, Wine's own server could end when a program closed, and a program that pauses one of its own threads waited for ever). Needs Nova 2026.11.11.2119 or newer.
- Folders are read much faster, which Windows programs do all the time.
- Windows programs trust the same web certificates as the rest of Nova. Without them Steam said "Steam needs to be online to update"; with them it downloads its update.

- Fixes DirectX programs freezing now and then with their picture stopped (the graphics card could be told that work was finished too soon, and then met commands that were being written again).
- `wine novagpu cube` says where it is if it stops drawing.
- `wine novagpu cube`: a turning cube drawn with shaders, to try real 3D through DirectX 11.
- Adds `novagpu`, a small Windows program that tries the graphics card: `wine novagpu vulkan`, `wine novagpu d3d11`, `wine novagpu window`.
- Fixes a program freezing when it lists the computer's drives (Notepad's Save As, then My Computer), and other calls whose yes-or-no arguments could be misread.

- The first package: Wine 11.0 as a command (`wine notepad`), 64-bit and 32-bit Windows programs in windows of their own, with sound.
- `wine --dxvk` puts DXVK and VKD3D-Proton in the prefix for DirectX through Vulkan; not yet seen working.
